existence.reason: While CSE701 covers AI in software engineering from a research and data-driven perspective (mining repositories, bug prediction), the new course focuses on modern AI-native software development workflows, coding agents, prompt/context engineering, and collaborative human-agent development.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct elective course.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 investigates AI techniques for software engineering research and repository mining, whereas the new course focuses on hands-on AI-native coding workflows, agentic tool use, and practical agent-assisted development.
CSE594A focuses primarily on agentic reasoning for algorithmic and mathematical problem solving, whereas this course is specifically tailored to software engineering workflows and coding agents.
CSE582 addresses traditional software evolution, maintenance, and product lines, whereas the new course examines modern AI-native software factories and iterative prompt/context engineering loops.
CSE581 covers traditional systems analysis and requirements engineering theories, whereas the new course focuses on executable specifications and spec-driven development with AI.
AI501 provides a broad foundational treatment of machine learning theory and algorithms, whereas the new course applies existing AI tools and agents specifically to software development.
CSE201 teaches foundational advanced programming and unit testing in Java, whereas the new course builds on top of these software engineering fundamentals to incorporate AI coding assistants.

resource_policy.reason: Because AI-native software development and coding agents are rapidly evolving fast-moving topics, a mixed approach using a foundational reference book alongside recent peer-reviewed papers, framework documentation, and book chapters is appropriate.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. Through structured lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions, students learn to configure AI coding assistants and developer workflows, construct agentic tools, Model Context Protocol integrations, and agent skills, assess executable specifications and development plans from requirements documents, analyze iterative development loops and software factory pipelines, and design automated evaluation frameworks for agent-assisted software systems. The course is designed for senior undergraduate students and emphasizes a workflow-oriented understanding through hands-on development and experimentation. It should NOT become a general introduction to AI or machine learning.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress from foundational AI-native development paradigms and workspace configuration to advanced agentic tooling, specification-driven requirements, iterative software factories, and reliability frameworks. This sequence builds directly upon the programming and software engineering fundamentals required from CSE201.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprises quizzes, assignments, reports, midsem and endsem examinations, and a practical project. This combination effectively measures both conceptual understanding and the students' ability to practically apply agent-assisted workflows, construct tools, and design evaluation frameworks matching the cognitive levels of the course outcomes.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701 which investigates AI techniques for software engineering research and repository mining, or CSE594A which focuses on agentic reasoning for algorithmic and mathematical problem solving, this course is specifically tailored to software engineering workflows, coding agents, and practical agent-assisted development.
